content.thinking:
The calibration is fast (0.3s) and the fabric build takes 2s. But the Dijkstra is trivially fast here because only 1024 vertices are finite — the graph is mostly unreachable! Why? Only node 0 is anchored, and the links connect (2m, 2m+1) pairs — so from node 0 you can reach node 1 (link 0) but not node 2 (link 1 connects nodes 2,3). So the graph is disconnected. Only 1024 vertices are reachable = 2 nodes × 512 phases ✓.

I need a connected topology for a realistic perf test. Let me make the links form a connected graph: e.g., link l connects node (l mod N) and node ((l+1) mod N) with slot (l // N) mod 8. With L=1024 and N=512: links 0..511 form a ring with slot 0, links 512..1023 form another ring with slot 1. Then each slice containing all 1024 links → each node has 4 ports in the slice (2 per ring: in and out) ✓.

Let me redo with a ring topology so everything is reachable. Then the Dijkstra will process all 262144 vertices and ~1M edges.

Let me re-time.
